clue.text: Songbird in distance behind rubbish

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so the distance word is placed second, after the rubbish word

blocks.note: chaff is husks and worthless stuff
an inch is a small distance

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher spots a songbird some way off behind a heap of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' places the distance word after the rubbish word, so this is a straight charade in that order.
explanation.definitionFit: The chaffinch is a common European finch known for its cheerful song.

clue.text: Stirring chorus we'd do with energy in band

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters are churned into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A band belts out a rousing chorus with plenty of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirring' reads as an adjective praising the chorus, but it signals the shuffle; the energy letter joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Crowded House is a pop-rock group from New Zealand and Australia, famous for 'Don't Dream It's Over'.

clue.text: Volunteers climbing with muscular movement in roof space

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: the TA, Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force
a tic is an involuntary muscle twitch

explanation.surface: Volunteers clamber up into a loft, one of them twitching nervously.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is the room or storage area directly under a house's roof.

clue.text: Routine following distribution of airmail

indicators.note: distributing spreads things around, so the letters are dealt out in a new order

blocks.note: f. is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Sorting the airmail has become a routine part of the postal job.
explanation.definitionFit: Something familiar is well known and everyday, just as a routine matter is ordinary and habitual.

clue.text: Reportedly understands instinct

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by how a word is spoken

blocks.note: to know something is to understand it, and the word is said like a facial feature

explanation.surface: Supposedly someone just grasps things by gut feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A nose for something is a natural talent for detecting it, as in a journalist's nose for a story.

clue.text: Elevated man protecting number on retreat northward

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround and shield it, so one piece wraps the other
in a down clue, going north means reading from the bottom up

blocks.note: he is the male pronoun
eight is a number
a den is a private retreat or hideaway

explanation.surface: A man shields a numbered unit as it retreats up the hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northward' only works in a down clue, where reading upwards turns a word around; 'on' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Heightened means raised higher, so it is a synonym of elevated.

clue.text: Club for spicy stuff

blocks.note: first meaning: a heavy spiked staff used as a weapon
second meaning: a spice made from the covering of nutmeg

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a club ordering hot food; the two halves are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a medieval weapon, a heavy club, and a warm spice derived from nutmeg husks.

clue.text: Inadequate part of wartime agreement

indicators.note: part of tells us the letters sit inside the following words, not built from them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A historian judges one section of a wartime treaty to be inadequate.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means scanty or insufficient, so it is a synonym of inadequate.

clue.text: Heavenly tea is prepared in small room

indicators.note: preparing something works it into shape, so the letters are reworked
in places the reworked letters inside the room word

blocks.note: a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A heavenly cuppa is brewed in a tiny monastic room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' does double service: it is part of the fodder, while 'Heavenly' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Celestial describes the sky or heaven, so it is a direct synonym of heavenly.

clue.text: Hopefully choose one film I name, last of trilogy

indicators.note: last of means we keep only the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: to opt is to choose
I is the Roman numeral for one
a mist is a thin film or haze
taken as written
to call someone something is to name them
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: Someone hopefully picks one film to name as the finale of a trilogy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' is not a movie here but a thin layer, as in a film of mist.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopefully and optimistically both describe acting while expecting a good outcome.

clue.text: Information about endless fervent love supplied in paradise

indicators.note: about means going around, so the information word surrounds the rest
endless means the final letter is cut off the next word

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
ardent means fervent or passionate
love is zero in tennis scoring, which looks like O
to feed is to supply with food

explanation.surface: Passionate love is said to have been provided in paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for information; love as O comes from tennis scoring, where zero is called love.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garden of Eden is the biblical paradise where Adam and Eve first lived.

clue.text: Easy to control party and country, not hard

indicators.note: not means the following letter is to be left out

blocks.note: a do is a party or social event
Chile is a South American country
H stands for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A guest at an embassy reception finds the country's people mild and easy to manage.
explanation.definitionFit: A docile person or animal is meek and submissive, so is easily managed.

clue.text: First couple of riders trapped in gorge with a magnetic quality

indicators.note: first couple means the opening two letters are kept
trapped in means held inside the other piece

blocks.note: a chasm is a deep gorge
the opening two letters of this word
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two riders are stuck in a ravine that seems to have a magnetic pull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'magnetic' tempts a physics reading, but the definition is the personal kind of attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is a compelling personal charm that draws people in, a figurative magnetism.

clue.text: Have a go at clues arranged in lists

indicators.note: arranging puts things into a fresh order, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An invitation to try clues set out in a list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have a go at clues' sounds like the solver's own task; only 'a go at clues' is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Catalogues are systematic lists of items, such as goods for sale or books in a library.

clue.text: Inspector joining fight, far from young, being ridiculed

blocks.note: DI is a Detective Inspector in the British police
to spar is to fight, as in boxing practice
aged means old, far from young

explanation.surface: An elderly police inspector who joins a brawl gets mocked for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To disparage is to belittle or mock, so being disparaged means being ridiculed.

clue.text: Frightening figure emerging from vehicle in moment before commotion

indicators.note: in puts the vehicle inside the moment word

blocks.note: a sec is a second, a moment
a car is a vehicle
a row is a noisy disturbance

explanation.surface: A scary figure leaps from a car just before a commotion breaks out.
explanation.walkthrough: Sec, short for second, is everyday British shorthand for a moment, as in 'wait a sec'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarecrow is a dummy set up in a field to frighten birds away from crops.

clue.text: Object to look after

blocks.note: first meaning: to be bothered by or take exception to
second meaning: to take care of, as with children

explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a noun, but here it is the verb, as in 'Would you object?'
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both raising an objection, as in 'do you mind?', and caring for something, as in minding a baby.

clue.text: Revised memoirs, omitting nothing, editor absorbed

indicators.note: a revised text is reworked, so the letters are put in a new order
omitting means leaving something out of the word

blocks.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, shaped like O
ed. is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An editor is engrossed in revising someone's memoirs.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove O from MEMOIRS, rearrange the rest, and add ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone immersed in a task is deeply engrossed in it, just as an absorbed person is.

clue.text: Work with a large gemstone

blocks.note: op. is short for opus, a work
taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A jeweller works on a big precious stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Opal is a milky iridescent mineral prized as a gem.

clue.text: Low tree man cultivated for fruit

indicators.note: cultivated land is worked over, so the letters are turned into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener grows a short tree to harvest its fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The watermelon is a large green-skinned fruit with juicy red flesh.

clue.text: Support airman with yen to make bequest

blocks.note: a leg supports a table or body
AC is Aircraftman, the lowest RAF rank
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A pilot backs a plan to leave money in Japanese currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A legacy is money or property left to someone in a will, which is a bequest.

clue.text: Framework in keel's warped by weight

indicators.note: warped timber is twisted out of shape, so these letters are bent into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe, then rearranged
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A boat's keel is bent out of shape by a heavy load.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton is a supporting structure, whether bones or the frame of a building.

clue.text: Substitute's story accepted by match official

indicators.note: being accepted means being taken inside, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: ref is short for referee
a story can be a falsehood, a lie

explanation.surface: A footballer coming off the bench spins a tale that the referee believes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Substitute's' means 'Substitute is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A relief is a person who takes over another's duty, a replacement or stand-in.

clue.text: Elements of wild fashion that are even seen in area near Washington

indicators.note: elements are component parts, so only some letters are taken
even positions mean the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

blocks.note: every second letter of these words, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Bits of outlandish fashion turn up in a district near the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Washington' suggests DC, but here it is the US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is a US state bordering Washington State to the east.

clue.text: Cheese in buffet available

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: Cheese is on offer at the buffet.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a crumbly white Greek cheese made from sheep's or goat's milk.

clue.text: Unreal disaster involved in tale of adventure

indicators.note: involved means tangled and complicated, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An improbable catastrophe features in an adventure story.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure Island is Robert Louis Stevenson's classic pirate adventure novel.

clue.text: Rock, southern style

blocks.note: S is short for southern
a way of doing things is a style

explanation.surface: Rock music played in a Southern style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' looks like the music genre, but it is the verb meaning to move to and fro.
explanation.definitionFit: To sway is to move gently from side to side, the motion of rocking.

clue.text: Resign and endure melancholy

blocks.note: to stand something is to endure it
feeling down is feeling sad

explanation.surface: Someone quits their post and bears their sadness.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand down is to withdraw from an office or position, which is to resign.
